reason: A fragment: the generic part 'appendage' (rejected in the 2026-11-13 review because it needs the organ it belongs to) run together with the quality present (PATO_0000467). The organ (connective, corolla lobe) is in the statement, not in this word.
Narrower: in Carex and Kobresia the cladoprophyll is the prophyll at the base of a lateral inflorescence branch. It is still a prophyll.

A shape word (deltate) plus the generic 'scale', which was already rejected. In these Helianthus rows the scales are pappus elements (PO_0025394, synonym 'pappus scale'), but the word alone does not say whose scales they are. 'Deltate' should be read as a shape of whatever organ the statement names.

target: portion of secretory tissue (PO_0005656), the gland of the Euphorbia cyathium; the appendage is the petal-like outer rim of that gland, a part of a stated whole (part-of pattern)
reason: Seen only in Euphorbia (FOC, Plazi). It is a real structure, but it belongs to one genus and the appendage can be stated as a part of the gland. A new class is not justified yet. If more floras turn it up, consider 'cyathial gland appendage' as a new class.

Narrower: the side petals (Polygala; the orchid petals other than the lip). The position 'lateral' has no value class yet (pattern 04, Limits), so the position is lost until the planned position values are released.

target: plant cell (PO_0009002) as part of the leaf; for mosses the whole is non-vascular leaf (PO_0025075), for vascular plants leaf lamina (PO_0020039) (part-of-a-whole pattern)
reason: Moss descriptions (Leucobryum, Bartramiopsis) of the cells of the leaf blade. PO has plant cell and the leaf classes but no leaf-lamina-cell class. The part-of pattern covers it.
Unclear: 'pollinia of 2 bony masses' (orchid pollen masses) versus 'masses ovulaires' (groups of ovules on a placenta in Pauridiantha). These are different structures and need the context.
Narrower: the outer whorl of tepals (Tulipa; in Eriocaulon the outer whorl is sepal-like). The position 'outer' has no value class yet (pattern 04, Limits).

A 'per X' counting phrase, like 'per node' and 'per axil' (rejected 2026-11-13). The counted part is the spikelet. The burr of Cenchrus is the bristly involucre (PO_0009100); a synonym rule could be added for statements about the burr itself.
A shape word (dot-like). The bearer is the cystolith named in the statement.
Describes how papillae are arranged. The number counts rows, not papillae, so grounding to papilla cell (PO_0025166) would give a wrong count. 'papilla' is already grounded by rule C269.
A quality: setose, PATO_0002289 (named in the previous review's 'setaceous' row). The setae themselves already ground to trichome (PO_0000282, synonym seta/setae).
A quality (thickened / épaissi). The parts in the statements are veins, a disc and thickenings of a named organ.
A fragment: trichome (PO_0000282) run together with present (PATO_0000467). 'trichome' already grounds.
The generic 'lobe' with a position word, like 'lateral lobe' (rejected 2026-11-13): it needs the organ (corolla lip, calyx, leaf). The position 'upper' also has no value class yet.
Narrower: the smallest veins of the leaf or leaflet blade, like 'veinlet' (rule C270), which also maps to the parent leaf lamina vein.

target: style branch (FLOPO_0986008), apex region (region pattern, as for plant organ apex FLOPO_0985023)
reason: The apex region of an existing FLOPO anatomy class. Asteraceae style-branch tips are subulate, truncate or penicillate.

Narrower: in Lamiaceae (Leonurus, Nepeta, Dracocephalum) the 'sessile oil globules' are sessile peltate glandular trichomes on the surface. They are not oil gland (PO_0005669), which is an internal cavity.

target: vascular bundle (PO_0005020) as part of glume (PO_0009039), lying between the keels (part-of-a-whole pattern)
reason: The veins of the lower glume between its two keels (Andropogon, Cymbopogon). 'nerve' maps to vascular bundle (rule C153); the glume is the whole. The count goes on the veins.
Exact match for vascular plants (Rhamnus), as with 'leaf vein' (rule C271). In moss floras (Campylopus) the leaf 'nerve' is the costa (PO_0030072); a rule by group should send bryophyte rows there.
Exact: a hyphenated spelling of 'leaf blade', which is a PO synonym of leaf lamina.

Covers two different structures: the scales inside the leaf sheath at the nodes of Hydrocharitaceae (Hydrilla, Ottelia) and the scale-like hairs at the nodes of Portulaca. Neither fits one existing class safely.

A misspelling of areolae. In Sphaerocarpos these are the meshes of the spore-wall network ('n areolae across the face'): a surface pattern of plant spore (PO_0025017), expressed as areolate (PATO_0002295). They are not a separate structure. The generic 'areole' was rejected 2026-11-13.

target: whole plant (PO_0000003; synonym gametophyte) with the context quality male (PATO_0000384) (pattern 04, state of the bearer)
reason: The male plant (gametophyte bearing antheridia) of the liverwort Sphaerocarpos, a narrower case of whole plant. Pattern 04 already lists male as a bearer state.
Narrower: in Schistidium the red rim is the edge of the moss capsule mouth. Moss floras only; it should not be applied to the rim of a capsule fruit.

target: costa (PO_0030072), its excurrent apex region (region pattern)
reason: In Bryum and Ptychostomum the costa runs out beyond the leaf blade as an awn, so this is the tip of the moss costa. It is not awn (PO_0025349), which is the grass and flower awn.
A size word plus a position word plus the generic 'cell' (rejected 2026-11-13). In Bucklandiella these are cells in a cross-section of the costa, but the whole they belong to is not in the word.
The noun for a quality: the costa running out beyond the leaf apex (excurrent). The bearer is the costa (PO_0030072) or leaf apex (PO_0020137) in the statement.
Unclear: in Dicranum it is the hyaline hair point of the moss leaf (an extension of leaf apex PO_0020137), while in Pectis it is the tip of a trichome (PO_0000282). The organ depends on the context.

target: plant cell (PO_0009002) as part of non-vascular leaf (PO_0025075), in the zone next to the costa (PO_0030072) (part-of-a-whole pattern)
reason: Moss leaf-blade cells beside the costa (Fissidens, Palamocladium). They are a group of leaf cells defined by where they sit, not a separate structure.
